q: Does the MPF-vs-Suzuki-4 crossover advantage predicted asymptotically by Childs-Wiebe persist quantitatively for physically-motivated Hamiltonians (transverse-field Ising, Fermi-Hubbard, small molecular electronic structure) at accessible sizes (n=6-14 qubits)?
basis: The current replication only tests toy 1-2 qubit generic Pauli Hamiltonians. The paper's engineering claim is about competitiveness vs S4 on real target Hamiltonians. We verified the ORDER lift, not the crossover point on any specific H.
next_steps: Implement H_TFIM = -J sum X_i X_{i+1} - h sum Z_i for n in {6,8,10,12}, run S1, S2, S4 (Suzuki-Trotter-4), and MPFs at matched target error 1e-3, 1e-4, 1e-5; log gate counts and total evolution time; find crossover t*(n,epsilon) where MPF wins on gate count. Repeat for 1D Fermi-Hubbard via Jordan-Wigner. Compare against modern qubitization gate counts to show whether 2012-LCU remains competitive or is strictly dominated.

q: How does the LCU / MPF primitive integrate with modern qubitization and QSVT: is a hybrid MPF-QSVT scheme ever advantageous, or does pure QSVT strictly dominate for large enough problems?
basis: The paper predates qubitization (Low-Chuang 2017) and QSVT (Gilyen-Su-Low-Wiebe 2019). The Lemma 2 subroutine is the same block-encoding primitive but the 2012 MPF construction is not embedded in the modern polynomial-transform framework. Whether MPF adds anything on top of QSVT is unresolved.
next_steps: Build a small block-encoding of H = TFIM (n=4-6 qubits) using qiskit or a custom stack; run QSVT-based simulation via Chebyshev / Jacobi-Anger for e^(-iHt); compare gate count and post-selection failure rate against Lemma-2 MPF for matched target error. Second: attempt a Richardson-in-degree extrapolation on QSVT polynomial approximants and check whether it lifts the effective order of a truncated Jacobi-Anger series analogously to how MPF lifts Trotter order.

q: What is the noise-robustness envelope of the LCU post-selection under realistic gate noise: at what depolarizing / coherent error rate does the failure-probability formula Delta^2 kappa / (kappa+1)^2 stop being a useful predictor of ancilla-measurement statistics?
basis: All numerics in this replication are ideal statevector. The exact-to-1e-9 agreement with the closed-form failure probability is a purely mathematical check. Real ancilla-postselected schemes accumulate noise on the controlled-U_a / U_b blocks that biases the ancilla-measurement branch.
next_steps: Reimplement the Lemma 2 circuit in a density-matrix simulator (qiskit-aer noise model or qutip). Sweep single-qubit depolarizing p in [1e-4, 1e-2] and 2-qubit gate error in [1e-3, 3e-2] (matching current superconducting hardware); measure empirical failure probability vs closed-form prediction, and fidelity of the success branch to the ideal (kappa U_a + U_b)|psi>. Identify the noise threshold at which post-selection no longer purifies faster than it accumulates error --- the practical MPF viability floor.

q: Can the Richardson-MPF construction be extended cleanly to time-dependent Hamiltonians H(t), and does the order lift survive under the Magnus / Dyson series treatment required?
basis: The 2012 paper treats time-independent H only. Real chemistry / control problems are time-dependent (Trotter product of ordered exponentials). Whether the negative-coefficient linear combination (- 1/3 S2(t) + 4/3 S2(t/2)^2) preserves its cancellation structure for a Magnus expansion is not addressed by the paper and not obvious.
next_steps: Take H(t) = (1-s(t)) H_start + s(t) H_final (a slow-schedule adiabatic Hamiltonian, n=2-4 qubits); implement a symmetric time-ordered S2-analog (midpoint Magnus-2); build the MPF Richardson combination; compare error scaling in the small-step limit against a fine-grid Dyson-series ground truth. If order fails to lift, characterize which Magnus commutator terms break the cancellation and whether a modified MPF coefficient set can restore it.

q: For the Pareto frontier of gate-count vs achieved error at fixed evolution time, where does MPF sit relative to S4 (Suzuki-4), S6 (Suzuki-6), tuned random-compiler (qDRIFT), and QSVT --- and does its position depend qualitatively on Hamiltonian sparsity / locality?
basis: The paper compares MPF asymptotically only to Suzuki formulas. Modern practice compares against qDRIFT (Campbell 2019) and QSVT/qubitization. No published all-method Pareto sweep exists for standard benchmark Hamiltonians. This replication generated only single-method traces.
next_steps: For each of three benchmark Hamiltonians (TFIM n=10, 1D Fermi-Hubbard n=6 sites, H2 STO-3G molecular Hamiltonian): sweep target error 1e-2 to 1e-6; for each of {S2, S4, S6, MPF/S2, MPF/S4, qDRIFT, QSVT}, count either exact 2-qubit gate count (if compiled) or number of controlled-Pauli exponentials; plot Pareto frontier (gate count vs error). Repeat with a sparse-versus-dense variant of the same lattice size to test whether MPF's advantage is a function of local commutator norms. Deliver a single figure that answers: does 2012 MPF remain on the Pareto frontier in 2026?
